subject: black swallower fish
title: A 7-Inch Fish Was Found With a 34-Inch Fish Inside It

scenes.text: This fish eats meals bigger than its own body. Then the meal fights back.
The black swallower. About ten inches long, and it lives nearly two miles down in the dark Atlantic.
In 2007, one washed up off Grand Cayman. It was 19 centimetres long. The snake mackerel inside it was 86. Four and a half times its length.
Hooked teeth swing inward to let the prey slide in, then lock. The stomach stretches until it hangs below the body, nearly transparent.
scenes.keywords: deep sea fish teeth close up

scenes.text: The catch: a meal that big rots before it digests. Gas builds up, the belly bursts, and the swallower floats up, dead.
That is how we know it exists at all. Almost every one ever studied was a fish that lost to its own dinner.

description:
The black swallower is a 25-centimetre deep-sea fish that can swallow prey more than twice its length and ten times its mass. In 2007 one was found off Grand Cayman, 19 centimetres long, with an 86-centimetre snake mackerel inside it.
Its hooked teeth fold back to let prey in, then lock, and its stomach stretches until it hangs below the body. Very large meals decompose before they digest, the gas floats the fish to the surface, and that is how most specimens have been found.
Would you eat something four times your own length? Comment below.

first_comment: The black swallower has rarely been seen alive, at 700 to 3,000 metres down. Nearly everything we know comes from dead ones that floated up with a meal still inside. Which deep-sea animal should we cover next?
